title: fix(ui): keep Undo available while a toast is focused or hovered
body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users lose the archive Undo toast after six seconds even while hovering over it or focusing its action with the keyboard.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared toast owner now pauses its existing expiry timer instead of making every caller manage interaction timing. Focus transfers between toast controls stay paused; explicit actions/dismissal, replacement, FIFO ordering, and modal relocation remain supported. True disconnection clears queued outcomes and timers. Existing archive Undo is unchanged; no new undo mechanism, persistent notification, stacking redesign, or global setting is introduced.

## User Impact

Users can pause to read and activate Undo without losing the action or their focus to an automatic timeout. The toast resumes its remaining lifetime only after both pointer hover and keyboard focus leave. No migration or settings changes.

Related: #128270 is the broader operator-notice presentation work. This PR is limited to the current shared toast’s interaction-aware expiry and its regressions; it does not take over that redesign.

## Evidence

- Baseline: nine existing toast tests passed. Six added interaction/cleanup regressions failed on the unchanged owner (focused Undo expired; hover/focus overlap timed out; replacement ignored retained focus; queued outcome outlived host removal).
- After: eighteen toast unit tests passed, including remaining-time precision, both hover/focus exit orders, internal focus transfer, FIFO/replacement, explicit action/dismiss, reduced motion, removed action focus, modal relocation, disconnection cleanup, and hover state reset after removal. Independent review caught the latter; a failing-before/passing-after regression now protects it.
- Chromium real-wall-clock component proof: baseline Undo disappeared around 6.6s while focused; fixed Undo remained focused beyond 6.5s and expired only after focus left plus its remaining lifetime. Actual shared toast and production styles with synthetic archive data; not full-app, mock-Gateway, or live-production E2E. Timestamped captures and assertions supplied with this change.

- Two existing Chromium toast layout tests passed; 48 archive/annotation caller tests passed.
- Changed-check guards, i18n, core-test typecheck, UI typecheck, and dead-export scans passed. The run found four missing test-only braces; those were corrected mechanically, then scoped oxlint (0 warnings/errors), stylelint, formatting, and all 18 toast tests passed.
- Independent autoreview: final P0–P2 scope clean after resolving its stale-hover finding. Full application build/live-Gateway proof was not run for this timer-only change.

### Before / after

Actual toast component, synthetic archive action, real elapsed time.

| Before: Undo disappears while focused | After: Undo stays while focused |
|---|---|
| ![Before at 6.6 seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8f4e38b-c5f3-46d5-845b-47ede03c328b) | ![After at 6.6 seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20097a30-4d5a-4f71-b3eb-84d9335fbfaf) |

After focus leaves, the remaining lifetime resumes and the toast expires normally:

![Normal expiry after interaction](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/555be204-fd6b-4bfc-86dc-dd5f1722933c)
